paraphrase: The tradition's charter: Śaṅkara established four āmnāya maṭhas — Śṛṅgeri (south; Yajurveda; 'ahaṃ brahmāsmi'; Sureśvara), Govardhana at Purī (east; Ṛgveda; 'prajñānaṃ brahma'; Padmapāda), Śāradā at Dvārakā (west; Sāmaveda; 'tat tvam asi'; Hastāmalaka) and Jyotirmaṭh (north; Atharvaveda; 'ayam ātmā brahma'; Toṭaka) — each with its sannyāsa names.
notes: Tradition's account; details vary between the maṭhas' versions; the Kāñcī maṭha's claim to a Śaṅkara foundation is a further tradition disputed by the others.
